notes.account: The page supplies a topological intuition for equisingularity over the complex base field. It proposes a tubular neighbourhood retracting onto X0, describes a fibrewise cone or mapping-cylinder model with boundary partial T, identifies its punctured part, asserts smooth-fibre and homotopy-equivalence properties, and presents a two-map diagram intended to reconstruct X. The last line begins a continuation about the functor varphi.

math_triggered_reading_decisions: The base of the cone description would naturally be X0, but the second phrase on L12 visibly says T sur X with no low 0. It is preserved literally.
The endpoint x mapped to (x,1) and the half-open interval [0,1[ were checked against the displayed quotient model; mathematics did not supply arrowheads where the ink remains doubtful.

The definition tilde X1=X1-T-ring was inspected because the subsequent boundary inclusion creates a literal set-membership problem under the stated closed-cylinder model. The circle over T and minus stroke remain as written.
notes.proof_scope: Two deliberately local checks are recorded below. No proof was attempted of the general equisingularity intuition, topological smoothness claim, complement homotopy equivalence, or homeomorphic reconstruction claim.

check_events.outcome: Consistent under the explicitly written mapping-cylinder model.
check_events.method: Let Q=((partial T × [0,1]) disjoint union X0)/((z,1)~p(z)). Away from the embedded X0, no identifications remain, so Q minus X0 identifies with partial T × [0,1[. The homotopy (z,s,u)↦(z,(1-u)s) stays in this product and retracts to partial T × {0}, preserving the X0-coordinate p(z). This verifies only the local punctured-cylinder identification and X0-homotopy assertion under this model.

check_events.outcome: Literal set-membership mismatch in the stated closed-cylinder model; no transcriptional repair made.
check_events.method: The previous model places the outer boundary partial T × {0} inside T minus X0=T-ring. The written definition tilde X1=X1 minus T-ring therefore removes that boundary from X1. Taken literally with these identifications, a map partial T→tilde X1 cannot be the asserted inclusion. This local check does not rule out an intended change of collar or an intended interior notation, neither of which is supplied by the page. Ink checked: the definition uses the same ringed T and a minus sign.
